q: A capacitor stores electrical energy in the form of an electric ____.
e: A capacitor stores electrical energy in the form of an electric field. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion.

q: When the capacitor is charged, the process can be viewed as the apparent ____ of charge between two conductors.
e: When the capacitor is charged, the process can be viewed as the apparent transfer of charge between two conductors. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates.

q: The charge has been transferred from a conductor at lower potential to a conductor at ____ potential.
e: The charge has been transferred from a conductor at lower potential to a conductor at higher potential. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates. A conductor lets charge drift when a potential difference is applied across it.
